judgment.notes: There are no external applications. Finite Cauchy–Schwarz applies to finitely supported shell restrictions and translated reflections, and to shell-index correlations after zero extension. Shell counting supplies the stated ell^1 costs. The geometric ratio is 2^(-1/2) in (0,1). Background notes BG002–BG005 verify these actual uses and their conditions.

S001 exhausts the positions of the two largest magnitudes; their ratio is at most 3, and the two alternatives in the mixed-pair case give 3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3. S002 correctly treats same-pair and different-pair placements. S003 obtains the unweighted shell bound by fixing the two smaller frequencies, then divides by N3>=2^j3. The gap j1-j2>=3 is incompatible with zero sum. S004 drops only nonnegative restrictions, bounds both correlations, and sums the geometric differences. Counting at most 24 permutations and three offsets gives, for example, the universal constant 144/(1-2^(-1/2)). S005 bounds every finite subsum by one finite truncation, so the supremum and every subset obey exactly the exported estimate.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
